question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis in the direction of decreasing $x$ where $x>0.$ When the displacement of $P$ from $O$ is $x\,m,$ its velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of its acceleration is ${3}^{1-x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,{m/s}^{2}$ and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$ If $v=-2\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when $x=2\,\text{m},$ find the velocity of $P$ when $x=1\,\text{m}.$ Round your answer to one decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14139845/assets/3c5450b18c5dc58b082faadf4086b6a21c0c9b55afb016090147609a2ccfe719.png)

Since the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle $P$ is ${3}^{1-x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-{3}^{1-x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3.
$$

Using the fact that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-{3}^{1-x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x & =\int [-{3}^{1-x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3]\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}={3}^{1-x}+C.
$$

Now, since $v=-2\sqrt{2}\,m/s$ when $x=2\,\text{m},$ we can find the value of the constant $C$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}(-2\sqrt{2})^{2} & ={3}^{1-2}+C \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{3}+C \\ C & =\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & ={3}^{1-x}+\frac{11}{3} \\ {v}^{2} & =2({3}^{1-x}+\frac{11}{3}) \\ v & =\pm \sqrt{2({3}^{1-x}+\frac{11}{3})}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the particle is moving in the direction of decreasing $x,$ we have that $v(x)<0,$ so we can discard the positive square root. Therefore,

$$
v=-\sqrt{2({3}^{1-x}+\frac{11}{3})}.
$$

Finally, the velocity of $P$ at $x=1$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =-\sqrt{2({3}^{1-1}+\frac{11}{3})} \\  & =-\sqrt{\frac{28}{3}} \\  & ≈-3.1\,\text{m/s},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
